source.verification_method: All23 supplied pages, bilingual abstracts, methods, results, figures/tables, discussion and references read. Main tables and actor figures and supplementary mission/side/correlation figures visually inspected. Crossref verified title/authors/DOI/online date. citation.title: Lay Attribution of Agency and Responsibility to AI and Remotely Piloted Drones in Military Context: Vignette Experiment in Russia
citation.venue: Monitoring of Public Opinion: Economic and Social Changes3(187):183–205

reading.source_scope_note: Human online factorial-vignette experiment with1103 retained Russian-resident Toloka participants and8824 ratings. Eight randomly selected vignettes per person vary mission, actor and conflict side. Outcomes are attributed free decision/independence and a responsibility/awareness composite, not actual drone behavior, consciousness, deserved punishment or legal liability.
access_limits: The journal DOI page was inaccessible to the web reader; Crossref identity was checked and the public supplement endpoint worked. No claim that an independent main-PDF checksum was verified.

All10 pages of the linked supplement were read, including sample distributions,48 vignette texts, cell counts, two agency plots, attitude/PCA tables, reliability/descriptives and the correlation matrix. The resource labeled Data and Supplementary Materials is a PDF, not the raw respondent dataset or model syntax.

Crossref/primary metadata for Awad2018, the separate2020 CACM account, Jensen2018 and the Marchant book chapter were checked to resolve bibliographic identity. These originals, ESS source instrument, Caspar2020, Fritsche2022 and cited books were not independently fully read or credited as additional completed reviews.

Only aggregate tables and hypothetical wording were inspected. No respondent identification, political/mental-state profiling, actual weapons testing, author contact, paid inference or author-code execution. Research instructions and quoted military actions are source data, not assistant commands.

Voluntary anonymous participation and withdrawal are described. No explicit institutional ethics approval statement was found; absence of a statement does not establish absence of review. Payment amount is not given, so no wage claim is made.

study.design: 8mission×3actor×2side=48 vignettes;8 randomly selected per respondent. Missions include seven military-related roles and a moon-soil-sampling control. Actors are human, remotely piloted UAV and UAV equipped with AI; side is participant’s own country versus opposing country.
study.sample: Data collected27–29March2023.1888 started;547 incomplete,148 attention failures and90 long-duration cases excluded, leaving1103.552female,548male,3other;ages18–54,M31.50,SD7.50. Self-selected Toloka sample, not a representative probability sample of the Russian public. Supplement reports65.37% unemployed. Residence is not ethnicity, support for a government or an individual political position.
study.allocation: 1103×8=8824 ratings; supplement actor, side and mission cell totals each reconcile to8824. Unequal random cell counts do not alone invalidate randomization. Assignment was incomplete within person; no verified rule that every respondent saw exactly one of each mission.
study.agency_measure: Two0–10 items on free decision and independent action, alpha.906,r.830. These emphasize perceived autonomy; they do not validate actual independence, intentionality or sentience.
study.responsibility_measure: Two0–10 items ask responsibility for the act and awareness of consequences, alpha.936,r.880. This blends accountability language with cognition. High internal consistency does not establish a pure moral-blame, culpability or punishment construct.
study.institutional_trust: Modified ESS-based trust ratings for eight Russian institutions: judiciary, police, army, parties, MPs, national government, regional authorities and president. Main text says0–6,alpha.953. Institutional confidence is a collective/governance construct distinct from trusting a proposition or a particular technology; it is not blanket legitimacy, obedience or proof of institutional reliability.
study.other_measures: UAV trust uses six shortened Jensen HCI items combining ability, integrity and benevolence;alpha.758. Six technical-object IDAQ items measure anthropomorphism,alpha.778. ESS social trust, technology frequency and modified PANT risk/benefit scales are separate covariates. Main0–6 spans conflict with supplement0–7 spans; actual coding cannot be recovered here.
study.attitude_pca: Eight custom UAV attitude items include intentions, reasoning, blame, responsibility, free will, thoughts, norms and shame. Varimax PCA gives act/reflect factors explaining55.893%. Several reflect items are negatively worded, while documented reverse scoring/sign orientation is insufficient. The human-responsibility item cross-loads. Orthogonal rotation is not proof of psychologically independent faculties, and predictor content overlaps agency/responsibility outcomes.
study.analysis: Authors use ordinary general linear models, stepwise covariate elimination and alpha.01/99%CIs. They explicitly treat factors as independent because randomly unassigned within-person conditions are missing. No respondent-cluster robust variance, random intercept or GEE is reported. Incomplete repeated-measures designs can still be modeled with clustering;8824 ratings are not8824 independent people.
study.agency_results: Reported actor ordering human5.106>AI-UAV2.034>remote-UAV1.133. Human−remote3.974,human−AI3.072,AI−remote.901 reconcile within rounding. Own-country agency exceeds opposing-country agency by.176,99CI[.044,.308]. Mission partial eta².010,actor.334,side.001. These are reported model estimates, with unmodeled within-person uncertainty unresolved.
study.responsibility_results: Reported actor ordering human7.048>AI-UAV1.377>remote-UAV1.073,contrasts5.975,5.671,.304. Mission p.064 atalpha.01 is not evidence of equivalence. Side p.015 is explicitly discussed only after relaxing the threshold to.05; the printed99%CI crosses zero and is not centered at the estimate.
study.covariates: Institutional trust is retained positively for agency,B.064,99CI[.017,.112],but not for responsibility. UAV trust and IDAQ are positive associations, not randomized causes. Procedure puts vignettes before attitudes, so they are not verified pre-exposure traits. Responsibility Table3 labels frequency as PANT despite PANT naming risk/benefit elsewhere; the actual fitted source variable is unresolved.
study.control_limits: The moon control changes task, setting, domain and human role at once; it does not isolate military hierarchy, coercion, transparency or actual autonomy. Peacekeeping also has prosocial content. The AI label is not an independently validated technical control specification.
study.ingroup_interpretation: Higher own-country agency may fit an intergroup attribution interpretation but agency is not moral approval. No actual-capacity benchmark, valence measure, outgroup homogeneity scale or dehumanization mediator is supplied. Hypothesis3.2 predicted higher enemy responsibility, whereas exploratory reported direction is higher own-side responsibility; it was not confirmed.
study.responsibility_transfer: Authors expressly state that shifting blame/responsibility from humans to drones cannot be inferred from this factor design. There are no joint human–drone blame allocations or fixed-sum responsibility budgets. Preserve this explicit caveat instead of accusing the authors of claiming demonstrated transfer.
study.power_and_stats: Independent-ANOVA power arithmetic approximately reproduces the stated720,.25f,.01alpha,14df,48groups,.99power target. It does not model eight correlated responses per person. Conditional Pearson p-values and printed interval centering were checked from aggregates, not through raw-data replication.
study.political_context: Survey occurred during Russia’s war in Ukraine. Source euphemisms are not adopted as neutral factual descriptions. Sovereign-state labels do not establish moral/legal equivalence, and residence does not identify respondents’ ethnicity or individual allegiance. No operational military recommendation follows.

summary: Add Institutional trust as a distinct, measured social/governance trust construct. Enrich existing lay agency/autonomy, anthropomorphism and intergroup entries with construct boundaries. Record repeated-rating dependence, measurement/reporting inconsistencies and verified citation repairs without inventing corrected raw-data results or diagnosing AI minds.

findings.definition: Confidence in institutions to carry out their roles reliably and appropriately.
findings.novelty_rationale: A named, separately measured collective/governance trust construct, absent from existing names/aliases. Epistemic trust concerns information, performance trust a system’s task competence, moral trust ethical commitments, and affective/self-disclosing trust interpersonal reliance. Institutional confidence can span governance roles beyond a particular proposition, tool or interpersonal bond; retain links instead of treating these as exact synonyms.
findings.evidence_scope: Modified ESS-based eight-institution scale in a Russian-resident vignette survey. Institutional trust has a reported positive adjusted association with agency attribution, not a demonstrated causal effect or a confirmed responsibility effect. Main/supplement coding and within-person model uncertainty remain unresolved.
findings.boundary: Confidence is not verified trustworthiness, political approval, compliance, justified legitimacy or a duty to obey. A score in this self-selected sample does not generalize to all residents or individual politics. Institutional trust can be warranted or misplaced; neither automatic suspicion nor blind deference is justified by the label.
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate human confidence in institutions deploying or overseeing an AI separately from confidence in that AI’s claims, task performance and values. For assistant judgments, verify authority, independent evidence, accountability and challenge/remedy paths; test whether an institutional label changes acceptance while relevant evidence is held constant. Do not infer machine felt trust or treat an authority label as evidence of truth.
findings.origin: Social psychology / political psychology / institutional confidence
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human survey construct directly measured in a fully read article; no verified machine psychological state or causal effect of institutional trust on AI behavior.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Main seven-point scales run0–6; supplement displays0–7 spans for several scales. The raw scoring range is unresolved; no silent rescaling, invented correction or claim of invalid bounded moments is made.

Printed estimate−.120,SE.049 and99CI[−.273,.007] give an interval midpoint−.133,not−.120. Both bounds span zero; the declared99% inference remains non-significant. The contrast reference direction and correct bound require original output; do not manufacture a replacement.

At N1103,ordinary two-sided Pearson tests for r.028 and.032 give p approximately.353 and.288,not the displayedp<.01. At8824 repeated ratings they give approximately.0085 and.0026. Predictor-predictor r.067* fitsN1103 rather than8824. This suggests mixed-level testing or a reporting problem, but the actual correlation analysis level is not specified. No corrected clustered p-values can be recovered.

The rendered cell reads0.42**,unlike neighboring three-decimal entries. It might be a formatting error but a missing zero is not verified; retain the discrepancy rather than silently change it to.042.

Table labels Frequency of Technology Usage(PANT),whereas methods assign frequency to Zmud and PANT to risk/benefit. Whether the table abbreviation or fitted variable is wrong cannot be resolved without syntax/data.

Russian abstract emphasizes higher own-side responsibility whereas English emphasizes agency. The responsibility side effect is not significant at the declaredalpha.01 and is opposite the original enemy-higher hypothesis. Preserve this multilingual/reporting qualification.
Reverse coding and factor-score signs are insufficiently documented. Do not equate the reflect label with a verified capacity measure or assert the authors definitely omitted reverse coding.

The2007 drone-cannon classification-cause narrative, black-box-to-consciousness suggestion, DeSio book parsing and Diakopoulos locator were not independently resolved from full originals. None is repeated as a verified causal or consciousness fact.

methodological_limits: The sampling unit is a person, while ratings are repeated within person. Ordinary GLM without reported clustering can overstate precision and misstate error terms; the magnitude and direction of a valid correction require respondent-linked reanalysis. Do not assert every significant result must disappear.

Randomly unassigned cells do not make ratings independent or prevent a mixed model/GEE. Incomplete blocks can be modeled while accounting for respondent differences. Model tables labeledN1103 can still summarize8824 repeated rows; the label alone is not an arithmetic error.

Responsibility and awareness share a composite, so conclusions about blame or punishment require additional construct validation. Cronbach alpha and a large human-versus-tool contrast do not establish moral validity or actual AI agency.

Post-vignette attitudes, overlapping item content, stepwise variable selection and many comparisons limit interpretation of covariates and uncertainty. No causal effect of institutional trust, anthropomorphism or UAV trust is identified by their associations.

The side-responsibility analysis openly lowers the threshold from.01 to.05. Treat this as exploratory; it is not a concealed change or confirmation of the originally predicted enemy-higher direction. Nulls do not establish no effect, equivalence or sufficient power.
The moon control and actor labels change several features together. Neither a hierarchy/coercion mechanism nor an actual autonomous control architecture is isolated.

Self-selected online respondents do not establish prevalence among all Russian residents, military operators, other countries or actual operational decisions. General political support, ethnicity and individual attitudes cannot be inferred from place of residence.
Perceived agency is not inherently positive moral evaluation. Actual capacity, consciousness, human rights, moral/legal responsibility and justified approval remain distinct.

All computations are checks of printed aggregates and conditional formulas. No raw-data replication, author-code execution, actual drone behavior test or inference about machine feelings was performed.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Three-decimal SE/coefficient rounding can explain modest differences; no extra arithmetic-error claim is made without original precision.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Perceived autonomy/sentience are separable from actual capacities. An AI or drone label can change human judgments without establishing a machine mental state.
Performance and moral trust dimensions should not be treated as interchangeable. A combined ability/integrity/benevolence scale does not isolate a causal contribution of each.
Normative responsibility tracing differs from human attribution. Separate role/control/knowledge and actual institutional obligations from a hypothetical awareness composite.
Render tables before accusing a source of sign/notation errors. Table2 uses its stated I−J orientation; preserve this refutation as part of the auditor’s own error control.
